summary: Sixth independent adversarial round over git diff origin/main...HEAD for the BUG_REPORT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL sanitizer. Verdict on the reviewed commit a9a0814: SHIP after one clause; no high/critical, 1 medium, 4 low (two of them pre-existing). Reviewer verified by EXECUTION, not reading: the 507 semantics down to the budget boundary (a sweep breaking at totalBytes<=budget can land exactly on the budget while Submit refuses at >=, so uploads stay refused — reproduced with a 200-byte budget probe), that no issue is created and no rate-limit token charged on that path, and that all six mutations of the systemd-hint condition die with a uniquely responsible test row each (the new tab-preceded row is the only thing killing the drop-'\t#' mutant). Also confirmed verbatim: every log string the docs tell operators to grep for, the journalctl-not-aurora.log claim against main.go handler ordering, install.sh carrying the bad env line forward, and the aurora.env WARN/silent enumeration against config.go. The medium was mine: the WARN enumeration said 'the first two are usually permissions' while the first item is a budget eviction, which is a capacity signal and never a permissions fault — an operator would have audited file ownership instead of raising the budget. Fixed in 5b2101f along with two low doc claims (the budget tunable does not WARN at startup like the four beside it; 'uncommenting a line is always safe' is true of setting lines but not prose bullets). THE POST-REVIEW DELTA a9a0814..5b2101f IS DOCUMENTATION ONLY — docs/bug-report-setup.md and scripts/aurora.env prose, zero .go files — so this record's verdict covers the reviewed code unchanged. Five earlier rounds are in the branch history (1 high + 3 med + 6 low; 3 med + 5 low; 2 med + 1 low-med + 4 low; 1 high + 1 med + 4 low; 1 med + 4 low), every one of which found either a doc claim contradicting the code or a new test that did not pin what it claimed. Known limits: the <=/>= budget asymmetry the docs now describe is not pinned by any test (no coverage exists on the 507 path at all), nothing pins docs against code so all six rounds of drift were catchable only by reading, and the booleans (BUG_REPORT_ENABLED=true '# on' reads as false and silently disables the feature) have the same inline-comment exposure and are deliberately out of scope.
